insights.insight: 91,438 cryptographically verified receipts representing $4.82M in confirmed GMV — this is deterministic purchase proof, not modeled intent. At ~359–398 receipts per day across live beta users, the panel is generating a consistent, auditable signal base.

Grocery-supermarkets (1,467 receipts, $63.8K GMV) and restaurants-dining (1,178 receipts, $36.1K GMV) dominate the 14-day window, with retail department stores and gas-convenience rounding out a top four that maps directly to CPG, QSR, and fuel brand planning cycles.

Three distinct brand entries in four days — McDonald's (QSR), Lowe's (home improvement), and H-E-B (Texas-dominant regional grocery) — indicate the verified panel is expanding across verticals and geographies, not consolidating around a single market or retail format.

Sixteen completed UTC days show ten clearing $94K and eight clearing $101K in pre-rollover GMV; the $94K level functions as a structural floor, giving brands a reliable minimum spend volume against which to calibrate audience sizing and campaign fit estimates.

The T20:15 UTC window (roughly mid-afternoon U.S. Eastern) has delivered 113–131 receipts and $4.7K–$6.1K GMV across three consecutive days — a repeatable intraday burst pattern that could inform dayparting strategy for brands activating against verified purchasers.

Standard programmatic buys $5+ CPM to infer purchase intent from behavioral proxies; a verified receipt confirms the transaction occurred, at a current cost of roughly $0.10 per receipt in the Crinkl protocol. The unit economics of deterministic confirmation sit an order of magnitude below probabilistic inference.
